title: Could Working From Home Solve the Global Fertility Crisis
author: Financial Times
summary: Research from King's College London, Stanford, and Princeton shows working from home increases fertility rates significantly. When both partners work from home at least one day weekly, total fertility increases 14 percent—equivalent to 0.32 children per woman. Women report the flexibility enables decisions to have additional children. Work location flexibility emerges as one of the most promising and cheapest fertility interventions available.
points: WFH at least 1 day/week correlates with higher fertility rates across 38 countries
Couples with both partners WFH have 14% higher fertility vs both commuting
Work flexibility closes gap between desired (2.1) and realized (1.7-1.8) family size
Flexibility identified as cheapest, most promising fertility intervention
Enables women in female-dominated sectors to plan additional children
quotes: Flexibility over where we work is emerging as one of the most promising and cheapest ways to help people have the families they say they want.
In richer countries women still say their ideal family size is a little above two, but actual fertility is stuck closer to 1.7 or 1.8.
Total fertility was "systematically higher for those who work from home at least one day a week"” Archived from Financial Times on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
